pāraṅgata.p: [ pāra + gamu + ta] (ti) Google Translate (1) Nirvana - the one who reaches the other side of the cycle. he. (2) The one who reaches the tip - the end - the peak - he. (3) The one who reaches the other side-outside.

R:
pāraṅgata：ပါရင်္ဂတ （တိ）
（နိဗ္ဗာန်တည်းဟူသော） တစ်ဖက်ကမ်းသို့ ရောက်သည်။
DOP: pāra n. [ ts ], the further bank or shore; the further side (of anything); (and iic: far, the furthest; the other side of); Abh 9 (nibbānaṃ … ~am api mutti …); 665 (~aṃ paramhi tīramhi); Vin III 16, 21 (tāva mahantā puñjā ahesuṃ orato ṭhito puriso ~ato ṭhitaṃ purisaṃ na passati); IV 113, 1 (~aṃ gacchanto nimujjati vā ummujjati vā); D I 244, 13 foll. (ayaṃ Aciravatī nadī … atha puriso āgaccheyya °’-atthiko °-gavesī °-gāmī ~aṃ taritukāmo, so … pārimaṃ tīraṃ avheyya ehi pārāpāraṃ ehi pārāpāran ti, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se ~ā ~aṃ; Sv 402, 27 : ambho ~a apāraṃ ehi); M I 134, 37 (na cāssa nāvā santāraṇī uttarasetu vā apārā ~aṃ gamanāya); S I 4, 21 (na maccudheyyassa tareyya ~aṃ; Spk I 27, 1 : tass’ eva ~aṃ nibbānaṃ); 52, 7* (te hi ~aṃ gamissanti chetvā jālaṃ va ambujo; Spk I 109, 24 : ~an ti nibbānaṃ); A II 51, 1* (~aṃ samuddassa tadāhu dūre); Dhp 385 (yassa ~aṃ apāraṃ vā pārāpāraṃ na vijjati; cf Dhp-a IV 141, 9 : ~an ti ajjhattikāni cha āyatanāni apāran ti bāhirāni cha āyatanāni); Sn 714 (na ~aṃ diguṇaṃ yanti); Ja I 57, 35 (rājā orato vā ~aṃ gacchati ~ato vā oraṃ āgacchati); V 491, 9* (taranti jātimaraṇassa ~aṃ; 491, 12´ : tebhūmakavaṭṭassa ~aṃ amatamahānibbānaṃ taranti pāpuṇanti); Nett 55, 7* (saccaṃ ca ~aṃ nipuṇaṃ sududdasaṃ … nibbānaṃ); Sp 1129, 23 (nadiyā ~e bhattaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ hoti); Ps III 160, 1 (asso vegena otaritvā ~aṃ gato, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se pāragato); Pj I 197, 25 (gaṅgāya orato ca ~ato ca aṭṭhayojano bhūmibhāgo); Dhp-a IV 141, 4 (pāpima kiṃ tava ~ena, taṃ hi vītarāgehi pattabban ti); Pj II 13, 2 foll. (avisesena hi ~an ti tīrassa nāmaṃ tasmā orāni ca tāni saṃsārasāgarassa pārabhūtāni cā ti katvā orapāran ti vuccati, atha vā … oran ti sakattabhāvo ~an ti parattabhāvo oraṃ vā cha ajjhattikāyatanāni ~aṃ cha bāhirāyatanāni, tathā oraṃ manussaloko ~aṃ devaloko …; cf also GDhp p. 202 ); — ifc see ora-; — pāraṃ, ind. , on the far bank; ? Ja II 160, 10* (alam etehi ambehi … yāni ~aṃ samuddassa); V 433, 8* (aguṇaṃ dhanu … ~aṃ nāvā … kicce jāte anatthacarāni bhavanti, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee wr cāraṃ; read ’natthacarāni bhonti with W.B. Bollée, 1970, p. 38 ?); — 2. an end or limit; the furthest reach or fullest extent; (and iic: the furthest); ~aṃ gacchati, goes to the end, masters to the utmost extent; Ja I 259, 12 (Takkasilāyaṃ sippaṃ uggaṇhitvā tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ ~aṃ gantvā); 303, 29 (sabbasippānaṃ ~aṃ gantvā); Vism 629, 35 (sammasanañāṇassa ~aṃ gantvā); Th-a III 171, 20 (yo bhikkhu pāraṅgato ~aṃ pariyantaṃ ukkaṃsaṃ gato); Cp-a 58, 15 (bodhisatto … sippesu ca vijjāṭṭhānesu ca ~aṃ agamāsi); — °’- aṇṇava , m. , the far side of the ocean; Mhv 5:58 (paccekabuddhaṃ taṃ khipa ~e); — °- kūla , n. , the far shore; Ap 559, 11 ; — °- koṭi , f. , the very highest point; Th-a III 105, 14 (sāvakañāṇassa pāramiṃ ~iṃ patto); — °- ga , mfn. [pāra + ga 2 ], 1. who goes to the far shore, who goes beyond; S IV 71, 24* (jātimaraṇassa ~ā; Spk II 382, 14 : jātimaraṇānaṃ pāraṃ nibbānaṃ gamakā hotha, Be, Se so; Ce gamaṇakā; Ee gamitā, prob. wr ); Sn 32; — 2. who has attained the highest point; who has mastered to the utmost extent; Ap 25, 30 (ahaṃ paññāya ~o); Mhv 37:215 (tīsu vedesu ~o); — °- gaṅgā , f. , the other side of the Ganges; S I 207, 20 (pādesu vā gahetvā ~āya khipissāmī ti) = Sn p. 32, 4 ; Ja II 159, 10 (~āya ambalabujādīnaṃ madhuraphalānaṃ anto natthi); VI 427, 27 (nāvāya ~aṃ gantvā); Sv 581, 21 (apāragaṅgāya bhikkhū Lohapāsāde sannipatiṃsu ~āya bhikkhū Tissamahāvihāre, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se paragaṅgāya); Pj II 227, 29 (~āya khipeyyan ti, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se paragaṅgāyaṃ); Mhv 10:49 (bhuñjassu ~aṃ tvaṃ); 25:2 (~aṃ gamissāmi); — °- gata , pāraṅgata, mfn. , 1. who has reached the far shore; M I 135, 10 (tiṇṇassa ~assa, Se so; Be, Ce, Ee pāraṅgatassa); S I 48, 3* (nāyūhati ~o hi so); A II 5, 29 (tiṇṇo ~o thale tiṭṭhati brāhmaṇo, Ce, Se so; Be, Ee pāraṅgato); III 69, 12* (te ve ~ā loke ye pattā āsavakkhayaṃ); IV 411, 1 (nicchātā nibbutā tiṇṇā ~ā); Dhp 414 (yo … saṃsāraṃ moham accagā tiṇṇo ~o jhāyī); Sn 21 (tiṇṇo ~o; Pj II 35, 12 : arahattaṃ patto); 803 (pāraṅgato na pacceti tādī; Nidd I 114, 5 : pāraṃ vuccati amataṃ nibbānaṃ; cf Nidd I 114, 8 : ~o pārappatto antagato antappatto koṭigato koṭippatto); Th 748 (ko so ~o loke, Se so; Be, Ce, Ee pāraṅgato); — 2. who has mastered to the utmost extent (+ gen. or loc.); Ja I 38, 30 (māṇavo tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ ~o va hutva); Vism 234, 19 ; It-a II 141, 19 (bhagavā … tapacariyāya ~o); Ap-a 377, 32 (sakkaṭavyākaraṇe vedattaye ca ~o); — pāraṅ- gama , mfn. , who goes to the far shore; S I 29, 5* (hīnattarūpā na ~ā te; Spk I 81, 6 : te nibbānaṅgamā na honti); — °- gavesi(n) , mfn. , seeking to reach the far shore; D I 245, 9 ; M II 64, 30* (alaṃ bālassa mohāya no ca ~ino) = Th 771 (Th-a III 36, 3 : vivaṭṭābhiratassa); Dhp 355; — °- gāmi(n) , mfn. , going to the far shore; going to the further side; S I 123, 16* (ye janā ~ino; Spk I 186, 3 : ye pi pāraṃ gatā … ye pi pāraṃ gacchissanti ye pi pāraṃ gantukāmā te pi ~ino) = Dhp 85; S IV 369, 11 (pāraṃ ca vo bhikkhave desissāmi ~iṃ ca maggaṃ); Ap 438, 26 (jantunā ~inā, Ee so, perhaps wr; Be, Ce, Se sāragāhinā); It-a I 172, 11 (jātiyā maraṇassa ca ~ino nibbānagāmino bhavathā ti); — °- gu , mfn. [pāra + gu 1 ], 1. who has gone to the far shore; who has gone beyond; S I 195, 8* (passe … muniṃ dukkhassa ~uṃ); Dhp 348 (bhavassa ~ū); It 33, 1* (jarāya ~uṃ); Sn 771 (nāvaṃ siñcitvā ~ū; cf Nidd I 20, 10 foll.: pāraṃ vuccati amataṃ nibbānaṃ …); — 2. who has mastered or understood to the utmost extent (+ gen. or loc.); D I 88, 5 (māṇavo … tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ ~ū); M II 144, 22* (~ū sabbadhammānaṃ; Ps III 397, 12 foll.: sabbesaṃ lokiyalokuttaradhammānaṃ abhiññāya pāragato, sabbadhamme abhijānitvā ṭhito ti attho); Dhp 384 (dvayesu dhammesu ~ū hoti brāhmaṇo); Ud 5, 8 (yadā sakesu dhammesu ~ū hoti brāhmaṇo; Ud-a 68, 25 foll.: ~ū ti pariññābhisamayapāripūrivasena pāraṅgato hoti … atha vā … tesaṃ sīlādīnaṃ pāripūriyā pāraṃ pariyantaṃ gato); Sn 699; Ja I 166, 18 (eko tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ ~ū disāpāmokkho ācariyo brāhmaṇo); Bv 2:200 (pañcābhiññāsu ~ū); Th-a II 94, 2 (brāhmaṇānaṃ vijjāsippesu ~ū hutvā); — °- vādika , mfn. , speaking of the far shore; Mhv 5:60 (Tisso so ~o; cf 5:58: paccekabuddhaṃ taṃ khipa pāraṇṇave); — apāra , mfn. and n. , 1. ( mfn. ) not having a (far) shore, unbounded; Mil 105, 11 (mahāsamuddaṃ … ~aṃ disvā); Bv-a 173, 15 (ākāso … ananto appameyyo ~o); — 2. ( n. ) not the far shore; the nearer bank; D II 89, 16 (app ekacce kullaṃ bandhanti ~ā pāraṃ gantukāmā, Be so; Ce orā pāraṃ; Ee wr aparāparaṃ; Se pārā pāraṃ) = Ud 90, 5 ; S V 24, 10 (aṭṭh’ ime bhikkhave dhammā bhāvitā … ~ā pāraṃ gamanāya saṃvattanti; Spk III 132, 17 : vaṭṭato nibbānaṃ); Sn 1129 (gacche pāraṃ ~ato; Nidd II 89, 19 : ~aṃ vuccati kilesā ca khandhā ca abhisaṅkhārā ca); Th 763 (~ā pāram esato); Ja III 230, 20* (atiṇṇaṃ yeva yācassu ~aṃ tāta nāvika; 230, 23´ foll.: paratīraṃ atiṇṇam eva janaṃ orimatīre ṭhitaṃ yeva vetanaṃ yācassu); — ~-pāragū, mfn. , who has reached the far shore of the unbounded (saṃsāra); Bv-a 1, 12* (apucchi satthāraṃ ~-pāraguṃ); — see also pāregaṅgaṃ.
